memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Israelites grieved for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days, until the time of weeping and mourning was over." — Deut 34:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When Moses died, the people did not rush past their loss. They grieved for thirty days — a full, unhurried season of mourning. Scripture records this simply and without embarrassment. Grief is not treated here as a lack of faith or something to be hidden. It is an honest, honouring response to the loss of someone deeply loved. The people gave themselves permission to weep, and God's Word makes room for their tears.

This is a gentle and important truth for us. When we lose someone we love, grief is right and good. It is not a sign of weak faith; it is love continuing to reach toward the one who is gone. The Bible never tells us to suppress our sorrow or pretend we are fine. It gives us permission to mourn, to weep, to take the time that grief requires.

Notice too that the grieving had a rhythm — "until the time of weeping and mourning was over." Grief is not endless; it has its season. There is a time to weep, and in God's grace, there also comes a time when the weight begins to lift. Both the mourning and the eventual easing are part of how God tends the human heart.

Jesus Himself wept at the grave of His friend Lazarus (John 11:35), showing us that tears and faith belong together. And He promises that for those who mourn, there is comfort (Matt 5:4), and one day a world where God "will wipe every tear from their eyes" (Rev 21:4). So if you are grieving, grieve honestly. God is near to the brokenhearted, and He walks with you through the season of tears toward the comfort He promises.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I allow myself, and others, to grieve honestly?
2. How does it help to know Scripture makes room for mourning?
3. Where do I need to bring my grief to the God who comforts?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You make room for grief and draw near to the brokenhearted. When I mourn, help me grieve honestly, and comfort me with the hope of the day when You will wipe away every tear. Amen.
